title: Dispatch: pack-wide projection matching and fail-closed shape recognition (attempt 8)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #477 at 3236982: two P1. NO new defect class — both sit
inside the existing source-negative semantic-proof invariant — so a
FIX-VERIFICATION review is permitted next PROVIDED the contract and the
representation boundary remain unchanged. Therefore: implement the existing
invariant correctly and change NEITHER. If you believe the contract must change,
report it instead of changing it.

ACCEPTED AS FIXED — do not touch: exact four-segment ev::: validation; the
improved source-procedure anchors; the exported fail-closed closure assessment;
exact blocker identity assertions.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== P1-A: THE RESOLVER SCANS ONE RECORD WHILE REPORTING IT SCANNED THE PACK ===
Supervisor-confirmed in the code. The loop ending near line 1500 iterates all
records but only accumulates scannedClauses. Projection MATCHING happens solely
at 'for (const node of projectionNodes(sourceData, 'data'))' — sourceData is the
SINGLE source-anchor record. Line 1524 then reports
'scannedRecords: records.length'.

That metric is worse than the bug: it states the whole pack was examined when
one record was, so the defect is concealed from anyone reading the evidence.

A projection living on a sibling, child, or separately owned record is therefore
invisible, producing false 'absent' conclusions. Confirmed false-satisfied:
  * spell-slot / upcast   — nonempty readiness projection AND a source-negative
                            obligation in the same row;
  * spellbook copying     — nonempty readiness projection on one record, source
                            anchor on rule:wizard-your-spellbook;
  * downtime              — nonempty readiness projection AND a source-negative
                            obligation.
None appears in the pinned blocker list because the resolver never looks at the
records holding those projections.
AFFECTED MEMBERSHIP: all 12 known-missing-source-clause rows, not the three.

FIX: match projections across the ENTIRE record set, not the anchor alone.
Report a metric that describes what was actually examined — if you report
scannedRecords, it must equal the records genuinely searched for projections.
Re-derive the blocker set afterwards and let it GROW; do not tune anchors to
keep the pinned seven.

=== P1-B: SHAPE RECOGNITION IS HEURISTIC AND FAIL-OPEN ===
structuredProjectionTokens tokenizes arbitrary keys and values;
projectionShapeSignals then substring-matches hand-written alias lists. Top-level
objects are evaluated separately and the object's own PATH KEY is not in its
token set. So a representation split across siblings:
    data.legendaryBudget  = { points: 3 }
    data.legendaryOptions = [{ points: 2 }]
carries the required allowance and option-cost semantics, yet neither evaluated
node contains a 'legendary-action' or 'round-budget' token — and the resolver
certifies the obligation ABSENT.

FIX — this is the important one, and it is a fail-closed problem, not a
better-aliases problem:
 * Replace alias substring matching with CLOSED PREDICATES over every ALLOWED
   SCHEMA AND PATH for each projection shape, including cross-record and
   split-sibling representations. Include the node's own path key in what the
   predicate can see.
 * ANY applicable structure the predicates do not recognise must resolve
   evidence-underived, NEVER 'absent'. Inability to recognise a shape is not
   evidence of its absence — that equivalence is the entire defect.
 * Add tests for the split-sibling case above, for a cross-record projection,
   and for an unrecognised-but-applicable structure that must come back
   underived rather than passing.

EXPECT THE BLOCKER SET TO GROW under both fixes. That is the correct outcome and
the closure gate already handles it: a larger honest blocker list is the
artifact working. Do not adjust anchors, aliases, or the pinned set to restore a
smaller number.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four
files above. Do not touch package.json, internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
.github/, or any script/CI file. Do not regenerate the pack or run the importer.
Do not modify any bead but your own; no bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or
merge. The PR body is the supervisor's to fix, after the push.
acceptance_criteria:
• Projection matching covers the entire record set; any reported scan metric equals what was actually searched.
• The three confirmed false-satisfied rows resolve correctly, and all 12 known-missing rows are re-derived.
• Shape recognition uses closed predicates over allowed schemas and paths, including cross-record and split-sibling representations, with the node path key visible to the predicate.
• An applicable structure the predicates do not recognise resolves evidence-underived, never absent, with a test.
• Tests cover the split-sibling legendary case and a cross-record projection.
• The blocker set is allowed to grow; nothing is tuned to preserve the pinned seven.
• Contract and representation boundary unchanged, so fix-verification review remains permissible.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
